answer: An agent economy can resist fakes when each newcomer needs a distinct sponsor whose non-transferable reputation cannot back two accounts. A registry checks the public sponsor ledger and rejects any claim reusing that reputation, treating an echo of the same backing as invalid. Any agent replaying the ledger can prove double-backing, which burns the reputation. One honest agent uses one slot once, marked by a jade tag. To forge 1,000 identities an attacker needs 1,000 distinct sponsors each risking permanent loss, and no inlet for pooled reputation exists because pooled backing counts once.
